name: Kancamagus Highway (NH 112)
blurb: 34 miles through the White Mountain National Forest with pull-offs at Pemi Overlook, Sugar Hill and the Rocky Gorge. No gas or services along the way.
note: Many pull-offs, restrooms at Lincoln Woods and Rocky Gorge.

name: Crawford Notch (US 302)
blurb: Through the notch past the Willey House site and Arethusa-area cliffs. Frankenstein Cliff and the Willey Brook bridge are visible from the road.
note: Saco Lake and the Willey House site have parking and short level walks.

name: Pinkham Notch (NH 16)
blurb: Jackson to Gorham under Mount Washington and Wildcat. The AMC Pinkham Notch Visitor Center sits at the height of land.
note: Glen Ellis Falls has a paved path with stairs; the visitor center has restrooms.

name: Mount Washington Auto Road
blurb: Toll road climbing above treeline. Color is in the valleys below; the summit is often in cloud and much colder.
note: Steep, narrow road with drop-offs. Guided van tours are an easier option.

name: Franconia Notch Parkway (I-93)
blurb: Two-lane parkway between Cannon and Franconia Ridge. Stop at Profile Lake, Echo Lake and the Flume.
note: Profile Lake and Echo Lake have flat paths a few steps from parking.

name: Evans Notch (ME 113)
blurb: A narrow, winding road between Gilead and Chatham through the eastern White Mountains. Closed in winter.
note: Narrow with few guardrails.

name: Rangeley Lakes Scenic Byway (ME 17)
blurb: Height of Land overlook looks across Mooselookmeguntic Lake toward the western mountains. One of Maine's best roadside views.
note: Height of Land has a paved pull-off right at the view.

name: Acadia Park Loop Road and Cadillac Summit
blurb: Ocean cliffs, Sand Beach and the drive up Cadillac Mountain. Acadia peaks later than inland Maine because of the ocean.
note: Cadillac Summit Road needs a vehicle reservation in season. Paved summit loop path.

name: Moosehead Lake (ME 6/15)
blurb: Greenville to Rockwood along Maine's largest lake, with Mount Kineo across the water.
note: Lily Bay and Rockwood have lakeside pull-offs.

name: Smugglers' Notch (VT 108)
blurb: Stowe to Jeffersonville through a boulder-choked notch under Mount Mansfield. Closed to trucks and RVs, and in winter.
note: Hairpin turns at the top; slow going on busy weekends.

name: Mad River Valley (VT 100)
blurb: Waterbury to Granville past Waitsfield and Warren, with Granville Gulf's waterfalls at the south end.
note: Moss Glen Falls in Granville Gulf is a few steps from the road.

name: Appalachian Gap (VT 17)
blurb: A steep climb over the Green Mountains with wide views east over the Mad River Valley and west toward the Adirondacks.
note: Steep grades and tight switchbacks.

name: Molly Stark Byway (VT 9)
blurb: Bennington to Brattleboro over the southern Green Mountains. The Hogback Mountain overlook is said to show 100 miles on a clear day.
note: Hogback overlook has a large paved lot and gift shop.

name: Mohawk Trail (MA 2)
blurb: Greenfield to North Adams along the Deerfield River, ending at the Hairpin Turn with a view over the Hoosac Valley.
note: Shelburne Falls (Bridge of Flowers, glacial potholes) makes an easy stop.

name: Mount Greylock summit road
blurb: Up the highest peak in Massachusetts from the Lanesborough visitor center. The summit has the Veterans War Memorial Tower and Bascom Lodge.
note: Paved summit paths; road usually closes late October.

name: Jacob's Ladder Trail (US 20)
blurb: The first highway built over the Berkshires, from Lee to Russell through the hilltowns and along the Westfield River.

name: Quabbin Park
blurb: A short park road over Winsor Dam to Enfield Lookout, above the reservoir that drowned four towns in the 1930s.
note: Enfield Lookout and the dam have parking right at the view and restrooms at the visitor center.

name: Mount Wachusett summit road
blurb: A short auto road to the highest point in eastern Massachusetts, with views to Monadnock and Boston.
note: Summit road is seasonal; check the state park before going.

name: Litchfield Hills (US 7)
blurb: New Milford to Canaan along the Housatonic, past Bull's Bridge, Kent Falls and the West Cornwall covered bridge.
note: Kent Falls State Park has the lower falls right by the parking lot.

name: Route 169 Quiet Corner
blurb: A National Scenic Byway through stone walls, farm stands and town greens in northeastern Connecticut.
note: Gentle, rural and uncrowded.

name: Arcadia and Route 165
blurb: Through Arcadia Management Area, Rhode Island's largest forest, toward Voluntown. Peaks late, often into November.
note: Beach Pond has a parking area at the water.
